#### 1. deficiency of adenosine deaminase 2  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.804)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5683826, Reactome:R-HSA-6798695)

**Proposed mechanism:** Adenosine Deaminase 2 (HGNC:1839) —DECREASES→ Reduced ADA2 enzymatic activity (HP:0001414); Reduced ADA2 enzymatic activity (HP:0001414) —DISRUPTS→ Cytokine dysregulation (GO:0001816); Cytokine dysregulation (GO:0001816) —INCREASES→ Inflammation (GO:0006955); Inflammation (GO:0006955) —LEADS_TO→ Vasculopathy (HP:0002677); Vasculopathy (HP:0002677) —LEADS_TO→ Stroke (HP:0001297); Vasculopathy (HP:0002677) —LEADS_TO→ Livedo reticularis (HP:0011191); Reduced ADA2 enzymatic activity (HP:0001414) —LEADS_TO→ Cataracts (HP:0000567). Loss-of-function mutations in ADA2 lead to reduced enzymatic activity, which in turn dysregulates cytokine production and promotes inflammation. This inflammatory process contributes to vasculopathy, manifesting as stroke and livedo reticularis in DADA2. In Sneddon syndrome, the reduced ADA2 activity also contributes to the development of cataracts, suggesting a shared pathway of inflammatory damage to the vasculature and lens.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in ADA2 (CECR1) with a clear gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect, or variants in completely distinct genetic pathways for one of the diseases, would falsify this shared loss-of-function mechanism. _(variant: rs149610965)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the dysregulated inflammatory pathways or restoring ADA2 enzyme activity could offer therapeutic strategies for both Sneddon syndrome and DADA2, potentially ameliorating shared vascular and other clinical manifestations.

Disruption of the NKX2-5 gene, a key regulator of cardiac development, leads to both conotruncal heart malformations and phenotypes associated with Sneddon syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of NKX2-5 variants in individuals with Sneddon syndrome, or demonstration that NKX2-5 variants do not impact cardiac development pathways in Sneddon syndrome patients. _(variant: rs114792716)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of NKX2-5 in these distinct conditions could lead to novel therapeutic strategies for both Sneddon syndrome and congenital heart defects, potentially involving gene therapy or small molecule modulators of cardiac development.

Dysregulation of the complement system can lead to vascular abnormalities, manifesting as Sneddon syndrome, and can also contribute to abnormal lung development and interstitial lung disease.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic loss-of-function variants in ADA2 in patients with Sneddon syndrome and interstitial lung disease 2 would support this hypothesis. Conversely, demonstrating that mutations in ADA2 only affect one of the diseases, or that distinct pathways are involved in each, would falsify it. _(variant: Common pathogenic variants in ADA2 (e.g., MAF > 0.01) in gnomAD would challenge a causal role in rare diseases.)_
